chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhary, from Roumi ibn Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A Christian man marries a Christian woman upon thirty kegs of wine and thirty pigs. Then they both become Muslim after that, and he did not enter with her. He (peace be upon him) said: He considers the value of the wine and the value of the pigs, so he sends it to her. Then he enters with her, and they are upon their first marriage.

key_terms.دَنّاً: A large cask or keg (unit of volume)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Christian couple's marriage if they convert to Islam before consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the Shia juristic principle of validating prior non-Muslim marriages upon conversion, provided the essential elements of consent and dowry (mahr) are preserved. By requiring the man to pay the equivalent value of the original dowry—wine and pigs, which were valid currency in their context—the Imam ensures the woman’s financial rights are respected despite the change in religious status. This ruling underscores the continuity of marital bonds and the practical application of Islamic justice in interfaith transitions.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Roumy Bin Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The Christian man marries the Christian woman upon thirty kegs of wine and thirty pigs. Then they both become Muslim after that, and he did not happen to have slept with her’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would consider how much the value of the wine was, and how much the value of the pigs were, so he would send equivalent to it to her. Then he would sleep with her, and they would both be upon their first marriage’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al- Jawhariy from Rumiy ibn Zurarah who has said the following: ‘This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who is a Christian and marries a Christian woman for thirty sacks of wine and thirty pigs; then they become Muslims and he has not yet gone to bed with her. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must find out how much the value of wine and pigs is. He must send them to her, then he can go to bed with her and they remain with their first marriage.’”
